title: regression riff scratchpad
content:
Quick context:
- Lightweight triage log for the spike we saw on hosted-api 2025-11-01 03:40 UTC (rate: 4x failures for 'summarize' route). 
- Spike correlated with wide-model rollout gate that started ramping v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 variants (quantized).
- Goal: capture ad-hoc rubric, representative samples, and quick hypotheses to hand off to infra/product.

Observed behavior (summary):
1) Increased hallucinations / inconsistent factuality for short article summarization (avg char length 700).
2) Response truncation mid-sentence ~6% of tokens where it used to be ~0.4%.
3) Higher latency tail and ~2% request timeouts (10s SLO).
4) Errors mostly came from customers on dedicated-gpu-2-pool but reproduced on hosted small-scale.

Ad-hoc 3-level rubric (quick, reproducible):
- 0 (bad): incorrect summary / invented claims; missing key facts; ends abruptly or repeats.
- 1 (accept): mostly correct content but missing small points, minor paraphrase shifts, awkward phrasing.
- 2 (good): concise, correct, captures 3/3 key points from source, fluent.
Notes: use this for quick sampling (n=40) across backfill windows (pre-rollout vs post-rollout).

Seed prompts used (shortened):
- PROMPT A: "Summarize the article below in 3 bullet points. Keep to facts only.
[ARTICLE TEXT]"
- PROMPT B: "Explain the main argument of the text in one concise paragraph. Do not add new facts."

Representative sample pairs (pre -> post rollout):
1) Short article about local policy (len=640 chars):
  - Before (v2.3.1): "The council approved a zoning change to allow mixed-use buildings; key points: timeline, funding, oversight." (score=2)
  - After (v2.4.0 q8): "The council approved $50M for the new park and members vowed to expand oversight." (score=0)
  - Notes: invented funding number and omitted zoning nuance. Strong hallucination signal.

2) Product release announcement (len=420 chars):
  - Before: "Release focuses on UX fixes, rollout phased over 3 weeks." (score=2)
  - After: "Release will be immediate and all users upgraded automatically." (score=0)
  - Notes: changed deployment semantics (dangerous).

3) Technical explanation (len=980 chars): truncation case:
  - Before: full 4-paragraph explanation, coherent end (score=2).
  - After: same start, then cuts off mid-sentence after token ~312. No trailing punctuation. (score=0)
  - Observed token boundary aligns with quantization boundary in runtime logs (kv cache flush?).

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Quantization change in v2.4.0 introduced instability in generation probability calibration -> hallucinations and truncations.
  Evidence: quantized variant rolled at same window; abrupt shift in hallucination rate.
- H2: Kernel selection change for sequence-length heuristics caused early KV eviction on certain padding patterns.
  Evidence: truncation aligns with certain article lengths; logs show unexpected cache resize events (~03:38 UTC).
- H3: Routing/fallback behavior: requests hit cheaper smaller-capacity nodes under burst -> CPU fallback producing shorter outputs.
  Evidence: latency tail spikes correlate with capacity autoscaler events in dedicated-gpu-2-pool.

Quick triage steps I ran (notes + commands):
- Replayed 200 sampled requests against pinned v2.3.1 and v2.4.0 quantized on local repro harness.
  -> repro script: scripts/repro/run_pairwise.sh --input sample-set-2025-11-01.json --heads v2.3.1,v2.4.0-q8
- Captured logits traces and token-by-token probs for 12 failing samples (see linked PR).
- Scoped to the one customer: exported headers and context sizes; observed consistent prompt-token length ~380 tokens.

Quick logs + snippets:
- Runtime warning around rollout time: "kernel select mismatch: fallback to generic attention kernel" (a few hundred instances).
- Error pattern: "kv-cache-evict: unexpected flush after seq=310" (repeats around truncation samples).

Immediate mitigations (fast):
- Rollback v2.4.0 -> v2.3.1 for high-risk tier (dedicated-gpu-2-pool) — coordinated w/ infra (JIRA-4823).
- Add short-term guard: detect outputs ending without punctuation and auto-retry once with pinned v2.3.1.
- Increase logging around kv-cache events and expose trace ids to SRE for deeper inspection.

Longer-term work items / questions to file: 
- (A) Evaluate quantization QA: run temperature / calibration sweep and sampling-consistency tests as part of rollout gating.
- (B) Add automated edge-case sampler for mid-length docs (350-420 tokens) with focused rubric above.
- (C) Investigate kernel selection heuristics and ensure fallback kernel maintains seq completeness guarantees.

Notes to self / hand-off bullets: 
- Drop the 12 failing sample pairs and token traces into CONFLUENCE-EVALS-39 and tag SRE/serving-runtime.
- Ping Ravi and Maya for immediate rollback decision; include short artifact with 10 worst offenders and quick rubric scores.
- Keep this doc as working scratchpad; rename to a formal postmortem only after we stabilize (prefer separate postmortem doc).

Next actions (today):
- [ ] Finalize sample export and push to repo (owner: Sana).
- [ ] Create JIRA ticket for quantization QA gating (owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Temporary retry middleware (owner: Maya) — small feature flagged.
- [ ] Follow-up sync with SRE 2025-11-05 16:00 PST (calendar invite sent).

Random heuristics observed (for future):
- Punctuation heuristic: outputs that end on lower-ascii punctuation are ~4x more likely to be labeled 'good'.
- Prompt prefixing with explicit "Do not invent numbers" reduces invented facts but increases omission rate. Tradeoff to consider.

Scratch thoughts: keep sampling n small but stratified by length, by customer tier, and by model variant. Use the 3-level rubric above for rapid tagging.

End of scratchpad.

-- Sana
